newsitem.title: TUNISIA: PLO welcomes Christopher presence at Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: PLO welcomes Christopher presence at Mideast talks.

text.p: The PLO said on Friday it would welcome U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher's attendance at Israeli-Palestinian talks this weekend aimed at preventing another outbreak of violence in the Middle East.

Diplomatic sources in Washington on Thursday said U.S. Mideast Coordinator Dennis Ross was discussing the arrangements with Israeli and Palestinian leaders. Some sources said the trip was extremely likely, but a final decision had not been made.
"We welcome any U.S. official who comes. We are ready if he (Christopher) decides to come," said Nabil abu Rdainah, spokesman for Palestinian Liberation Organisation President Yasser Arafat.

The plan would be for Christopher to leave Washington for Israel on Saturday and be present for the start of the talks on Sunday at the border crossing of Erez between Israel and the Palestinian self-rule region of Gaza.
The two-day Washington crisis summit called by President Bill Clinton this week involved Israel's hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Arafat.
It ended on Wednesday with no agreement on major substantive issues that led to fierce violence last week, threatening to further undermine the already battered peace process.

The only achievement of the summit -- a limited one that promoted Palestinians and other critics to brand it a failure -- was an agreement for the two sides to resume open-ended negotiations on Sunday.
